original_forecast.resolution_rule: Use only the FIRST Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index for October 2026 (scheduled Tuesday November 10, 2026 at 08:30 EST). The series is seasonally adjusted CPI-U all items less food and energy monthly percentage change, at first-release BLS one-decimal percentage-point precision. TRUE iff first reported core CPI monthly change is >=+0.4%, otherwise FALSE. If BLS does not publish this specific month-over-month figure in the first release, remain PENDING and record non-resolution; do not substitute YoY rates, core PCE, revisions, forecasts, or imputed unpublished figures. Score frozen p=.30 by Brier/log loss; also point +0.3%, nominal 80% [0.1%,0.5%] and fixed +0.3% September first-release and attributed external point benchmarks separately. If official release is delayed, defer resolution to first actual publication; no forecast edits.
rationale: Recent October total payroll growth +165K and strong services demand make broad price-pressure propagation possible, but do not directly measure prices; H003 increases core-tail risk.

September first core CPI was +0.3% m/m, and professional estimates range from ~+0.21% (earlier TD report) to +0.3% (RBC), so the >=+0.4% threshold is deliberately an upside-core surprise event rather than a base case.

Preliminary Michigan 1-year inflation expectations eased to 4.3% from 4.7% despite low sentiment; survey expectations are not measured October CPI and cannot substitute for the official first release.

Energy-driven headline inflation can coexist with contained core prices. The p=.30 is a judgmental distributional forecast under v0.2.21, not empirically calibrated within a homogeneous target family.
Some October 2025 annual comparison series are unavailable due to 2025 shutdown; therefore only October 2026 month-over-month core CPI is the target.
surprising_if: Core CPI first print >=+0.5% m/m, above forecast upper central expectation and strongly challenging contained-core model.
Core CPI first print <=+0.1% m/m, consistent with rapid core deceleration despite high nominal demand and input-price surveys.
original_forecast.source_timing_note: Only information available by evidence cutoff is used; score from first future BLS publication. The model did not foresee the current payroll surprise; P000034's failure is not overwritten by this new test.

resolution.audit_note: Auditor-only application of the frozen Nov 6 event: first BLS October core CPI seasonally adjusted m/m +0.3% at one-decimal precision, below >=0.4% threshold; event FALSE, p=.30 Brier .09 log loss .356675. Frozen point +.3 exact and 80% [.1,.5] covers. September and attributed RBC point .3 also exact; no model advantage over those points. Headline +.4 is a different series and does not resolve core event. No later revisions or model interpretations entered original.
